subject: I-O-CONTROL paragraph
notes: The format is `I-O-CONTROL . [[apply-commit-clause].] [[{same-clause}...].]`, RENDERED from the printed page (PDF p363 / printed folio 333); the prose under the figure adds that the two clauses may be specified in any order. kb/Work PB2727: the run of SAME clauses is ONE sentence closed by ONE separator period and the APPLY COMMIT clause a sentence of its own; the grammar's `(ioControlClause DOT?)*` is a punctuation superset read by ClosedFormatPass through ParagraphPeriods, which refuses a period splitting a sentence (COBOL3407) or a missing closing one (COBOL3408) at every edition — a period after each clause used to compile clean. Both clauses are modelled: same-clause with all of its RECORD / SORT / SORT-MERGE variants, and apply-commit-clause bound for every file 9.1.18.2 admits (Annex A.4.3; kb/Work PB3338, PB3340: COBOL1709, the earlier refusal by name, is retired). The COBOL-85 RERUN and MULTIPLE FILE TAPE clauses removed at COBOL-2002 are superset-parsed and removal-gated post-bind. The residue is now DIAGNOSED: this alternative list ended in an INLINE generic-clause catch-all, which is why kb/Work PB487's sibling sweep — reading the grammar by rule NAME — never counted it, and `I-O-CONTROL.` followed by `WIBBLE WOBBLE.` compiled and ran in silence. It is now the shared `unrecognizedClause` error production, COBOL1970.
